system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: we set up system prompts and instance prompts for each agent role. The system prompt primarily describes the definition of role identity, role responsibilities, and corresponding actions.
system_prompt_style.note: Per-role prompts (config/roles/*.yml exist but contents not in evidence); instance prompt includes raw issue. Paper-only mechanism.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: We use a simple linear combination here to calculate the final suspiciousness score from both methods.
env_context_strategy.note: BM25+SBFL fault localization results injected into prompt, plus agent-driven search/open actions (Table 1).

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The Reproducer role similarly uses nucleus sampling, but only incorporates the last five histories.
context_compaction.note: Last-N history window per role; Manager uses full history. Also summary reports between agents (Action 21).

observation_format.evidence_quote: Action 22 provides basic Linux shell commands such as “cd”, “ls”, “grep”, and “cat”.

tool_call_format.note: No parser code in repo evidence; figure shows 'Thought:/Action:' text format (SWE-agent style) but mechanism unverified.

tool_count.evidence_quote: Actions selected and designed for each agent. 1-10 are from SWE-agent and 11-17 are from AutoCoderRover.
tool_count.note: Actions 0-22 across all roles; per-role subsets smaller.

edit_primitive.note: SWE-agent style edit; create action also listed.

tool_schema_source.note: Tool definition files not in evidence.

protocol_standardization.note: No source code or dependency files in evidence.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the specified agent will start to execute its sub-task using the ReAct framework [15] iteratively.
loop_primitives.note: Pre-defined task graphs; Plan C adds test feedback loop (generate_test_repair) but only Plans A/B used.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: For plans, we design a graph data structure that can be parsed and strictly executed.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: our design contains five agents, which can collaboratively solve GitHub issues:
multi_agent_topology.note: Manager selects plan; agents hand off via task graph; orchestrator_workers also plausible.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: all actions that the agent performed will be summarized and passed to its “downstream” according to the result of the current sub-task.

human_in_loop.note: Paper mentions plan injection from humans but no runtime gating; no code.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Plans in Figure 2 will be parsed into a graph with an entry node specified by “entry”.

long_term_memory.note: Action 18 retrieves similar issues from a corpus; no code to verify persistence.

state_persistence.note: Paper says restart from beginning on crash; no code.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Verifier: The verifier is an agent that will run the reproduced or integration tests3 to check whether the modifications have resolved the issue or not.

retry_policy.note: Manager may come up with new plan or give up; no code.

rollback.note: Files restored after localization per paper Sec. 4.1.1; no code.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The plan finishes when the Manager is activated or exceeds our budget.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: we set the maximum cost to 8$ per issue.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We pre-construct an environment-completed docker image offline to avoid wasting time on real-time installation during inference.

permission_model.evidence_quote: We assign a unique set of actions to each role, similar to how different roles in the real world possess distinct skills.
permission_model.note: Per-role action sets; not a command blocklist.

eval_hooks.note: Repo ships eval logs/results only, no harness code.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Repair & Resolve reported bugs and add new features within code Repository.

open_source.note: Repo contains only role configs, predictions, logs, trajectories; no harness source code or LICENSE in tree.

model_agnostic.note: Only GPT-4 used; no client code.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Detailed prompt engineering designs for CODE R can be found at https://github.com/NL2Code/CodeR.

first_release_date.note: No tags in evidence; README release date.

stars.note: Date of star count not stated.
